lines.text: In most states, lemon laws don't cover used cars.
lines.say: In most states, lemon laws don't cover used cars.

lines.text: Only about 10 states have a used-car lemon law, like New York and Massachusetts.
lines.say: Only about ten states have a used-car lemon law, like New York and Massachusetts.

lines.text: New cars differ: all 50 states have one. If a serious defect survives too many repairs, the maker refunds or replaces the car.
lines.say: New cars differ: all fifty states have one. If a serious defect survives too many repairs, the maker refunds or replaces the car.

lines.text: California, for example, presumes a lemon within 18 months or 18,000 miles: 4 repair tries, or over 30 days in the shop.
lines.say: California, for example, presumes a lemon within eighteen months or eighteen thousand miles: four repair tries, or over thirty days in the shop.

lines.text: Not covered: accident damage, abuse or neglect, unauthorized mods, and minor defects.
lines.say: What's not covered? Accident damage, abuse or neglect, unauthorized modifications, and minor defects.

lines.text: A buyback isn't a full refund. Hypothetical California example: a $50,000 car first repaired at 6,000 miles loses a $2,500 usage offset.
lines.say: A buyback isn't a full refund. Hypothetically, in California, a fifty-thousand-dollar car first repaired at six thousand miles loses a two-thousand-five-hundred-dollar usage offset.

lines.text: Used car with a written warranty? Federal Magnuson-Moss law makes it enforceable.
lines.say: Used car with a written warranty? The federal Magnuson-Moss Act makes it enforceable.

lines.text: In California, winning buyers get attorney fees paid by the maker.
lines.say: In California, winning buyers get attorney fees paid by the maker.

post.title: Lemon laws skip used cars in most states. Here's why
post.ig:
In most states, lemon laws don't cover used cars.
About 10 states have used-car lemon laws, including New York and Massachusetts.
All 50 states cover new cars: in California, 4 repair tries or 30+ days in the shop within 18 months/18,000 miles presumes a lemon.
A buyback isn't a full refund: California subtracts a usage offset (hypothetical: $2,500 on a $50,000 car first repaired at 6,000 miles).
Sources: CA Civil Code 1793.22, NY Attorney General, J.D. Power, FTC.
